title: How To Catch Sneaky Students https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2026/09/25/teacher-catch-sneaky-misbehaving-students/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin addresses the moment a teacher senses misbehavior behind their back but does not know who did it. He argues that the common reaction of spinning around, glaring and threatening guarantees the behavior will return, because sneaky students enjoy the thrill and the attention. His first principle is vigilant supervision, positioning yourself so the class is in front of you until students swear you have eyes in the back of your head. When something still slips through, the counterintuitive move is to feign ignorance, avoid flinching or turning, and position the disruption off to one side. Because impulsive students cannot resist repeating it, you use peripheral vision and hearing to catch the second occurrence in the act. The payoff is that waiting calmly lets you see the whole scene play out.
points: Spinning around, glaring and threatening teaches sneaky students that misbehavior gets attention, so it nearly guarantees a repeat.
Strong supervision starts with positioning so the class is always in front of you, making students feel you see everything.
When something slips past you, feign ignorance and do not flinch or turn toward the rule-breakers.
Impulsive students almost always repeat the behavior within seconds, which lets you catch it with peripheral vision.
Keeping your cool and waiting turns a missed incident into a clear, witnessed one without confrontation.
quotes: If you’re like most teachers, you spin around and glare. You ask who did it. You threaten that it better not happen again.
Because sneaky students like the thrill of it. They like the attention of their classmates. And the more you miss their misbehavior, the more fun it is.
Good teachers position themselves. They keep their class in front of them like K-pop concert security.
Alert supervision will demoralize even the stealthiest house mouse. Why even bother misbehaving if the teacher is always right there watching and noticing it all.
Well, if you were to shrewdly pretend not to notice, it would happen again and within seconds. Because sneaky students can’t resist; their impulsivity always gets the better of them.
Don’t flinch. Don’t turn and face the rule-breaker(s). Act as if nothing happened.
A phone being passed. An eraser being thrown. A joke shared and laughed at. Busted. Like candy from a baby. As long as you keep your cool and wait, they always do it again.
